output.title: Design out the error that feeds itself
output.body:
When a workflow keeps correcting its own mistakes, the problem is usually not the last error. It is the loop that sends bad data back into the same process.

A useful bounded question is: which repeated manual task creates the next round of rework? For example, if invoice details are entered by hand and later reconciled by hand because the first entry was incomplete or misclassified, the workflow is teaching itself to repeat the same mistake. That is the loop to design against.

The practical next step is not to automate everything. Start with a simple fit check: is the work repetitive, does it happen often enough to matter, does it already live in digital documents or SaaS tools, and do you control the process change? If the answer is no, AI probably does not belong there yet. Better to change the process than bolt software onto a bad one.

If the answer is yes, define one error-blocking control before anything else. That might be duplicate detection, mandatory field validation, or human approval before a high-risk step. The system should catch the mistake before it gets a chance to cycle back. Human approval stays in place for money movement and any other high-risk decision. Boring, but effective, which is usually the point.

Then scope a small pilot around one workflow and one control. Keep the success measure concrete enough that you can tell whether the rework loop actually broke, without pretending the whole business needs a full rebuild.
